newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Russian space probe expected to land in outback.
newsitem.headline: Russian space probe expected to land in outback.

text.p: Russia's stricken Mars probe was expected to crash about 360 km (220 miles) north of the outback Australian town of Broken Hill about 0110 GMT on Monday, defence authorities said.
The six-tonne probe is carrying four canisters of potentially lethal plutonium.
Broken Hill is an isolated mining town about 900 km (560 miles) west of Sydney, Australia's largest city.
Emergency Management Australia spokesman David Cregan told Reuters said authorities were monitoring the situation and their latest estimate was still imprecise.
Emergency Management Australia, a unit of the Defence Department, is responsible for implementing the emergency plan for dealing with the impact of space debris.

Russian authorities have assured the Australian government the plutonium canisters were designed to withstand the impact of re-entry into the earth's atmosphere and the impact of a crash, Prime Minister John Howard told reporters earlier.
